nodes.rationale: Commercial license terms must be verified before shipping.

nodes.label: entitlements Table
nodes.rationale: One entitlement per user regardless of store; writable only by the service role.

nodes.label: Flight Lookup Provider
nodes.rationale: Paid per call, so it stays server-side only, is cached aggressively and is limited for free users.

nodes.label: Wingspot Pro Subscription
nodes.rationale: Pro is tied to the Wingspot account, not to the store, so it unlocks on every platform.

nodes.label: Cross-platform Contract Rules
nodes.rationale: iOS and Android ship at different times, so versioning, minimum versions and per-platform feature flags keep the backend from assuming both have a feature.

nodes.label: Reference Data
nodes.rationale: The app lives or dies on good aircraft and airport data; registration mapping is the biggest effort.

nodes.label: Trustworthy Progress Principle
nodes.rationale: Verified check-ins make badges mean something.

nodes.label: Boarding Pass Scan
nodes.rationale: Runs fully on-device; passenger name and PNR are never stored or uploaded.

nodes.label: Monorepo Layout
nodes.rationale: Path-filtered CI runs both apps and the backend on contract changes, so a breaking API change fails before it ships.

nodes.label: CloudKit (Ruled Out)
nodes.rationale: Ties the social graph to Apple accounts and rules out Android.

nodes.label: Firebase (Alternative)
nodes.rationale: Cross-platform, but aggregations and geo queries are awkward in Firestore and cost more at scale.

nodes.label: On-device SQLite Snapshot
nodes.rationale: One versioned file with FTS5 search is used by both apps and updated through weekly deltas.

nodes.label: Safety, Privacy and Legal Rules
nodes.rationale: Spotting is legally sensitive in some countries, so public check-ins never expose raw GPS and sensitive aircraft can be hidden.

nodes.label: Supabase
nodes.rationale: Has first-party Swift and Kotlin SDKs, keeps logic in Postgres and Edge Functions for both clients, and relational data plus PostGIS fit badge aggregates and geofences.

nodes.label: Core Loop (See, Check In, Reward, Social)
nodes.norm_label: core loop (see, check in, reward, social)
nodes.rationale: Badges and check-ins are never paywalled because they are the core loop and the social proof.

nodes.label: Client Badge Progress Predictor
nodes.rationale: Gives instant feedback from local data while badge evaluation stays server-authoritative.

nodes.label: Offline Outbox Sync
nodes.rationale: Check-in IDs are UUIDv7 generated on the device, so retries are idempotent.

nodes.label: Roadmap (iOS First, Android Second)
nodes.rationale: A solo or small team should not build two apps in parallel before the core loop is proven.

nodes.label: Android App (Kotlin / Jetpack Compose)
nodes.rationale: Starts only after the iOS MVP, in Phase 2b.

nodes.label: Badge Engine (Rules as Data)
nodes.rationale: Badges are JSON rules evaluated server-side, so new badges and seasonal events ship without an app update.

nodes.label: Client Write Rule (Edge Functions Only)
nodes.rationale: Every write with business logic goes through an Edge Function to keep rules in one place instead of two clients.

nodes.label: Offline First Principle
nodes.rationale: Spotting spots and aircraft cabins have bad reception, so everything must work offline and sync later.

nodes.label: One Backend, Native Clients Principle
nodes.rationale: All business rules live on the server; clients only render, cache and predict, so nothing in the backend depends on a single platform.

nodes.label: Airport Visit Check-in
nodes.rationale: Implicitly created by spotted and flown check-ins so users do not have to double log.
